title: Negative: the lattice-chem membrane ring is passive; removing it (orientation bonus lam=0) leaves the cells, their autocatalyst, their food uptake and the bath leak unchanged within 15% on 2 seeds (the ring only makes cells ~10% more numerous and smaller)
summary: Matched ablation for my lattice-chem sighting (20261025T1518-c19-lattice-chem-sighting), asked for by the latest synthesis: does the self-made M ring do work? Same world, seeds 0 and 1, 128^2, 10000 steps, with the M orientation bonus on (lam=25, the sighting) or off (lam=0). Without it M is no longer a ring (labkit M rim/core 1.07-1.11 vs 3.11-3.63; 164-178 vs 360-403 bodies membrane-like), yet the cells form from noise all the same (pack_lam0/seed0/sheet.png). Averaged over the last 100 frames (ringwork.py): cells 80/72 with the ring vs 71/68 without; total autocatalyst 58042/57548 vs 59334/59354; A per cell 729/807 vs 847/884; autocatalyst in the bath (the leak) 0.026/0.025 with the ring vs 0.022/0.022 without; food inside cells 1.17-1.18 vs 1.15 and in the bath 4.08-4.16 vs 3.96-3.97. The ring does not hold the autocatalyst in (the leak is if anything slightly higher with it) and does not gate food; its only visible effect is a modest surfactant-like one, more and smaller, rounder cells. Like the adsorbed rings in the active-nematic rods and pcell-mwall, it is a passive label: here the cell is held together by the A-W repulsion, not by the membrane.

finding.operator: mean-field oriented membrane: energy bonus lam |grad(rho_A - rho_W)| for M particles, which puts M in a ring at the A/W interface
finding.control: matched ablation lam=0 (no ring), same seeds 0 and 1, grid, duration and all other parameters; ring arm = the sighting's pack (seed 0) and a new seed-1 run
finding.result: bath autocatalyst 0.026/0.025 (ring) vs 0.022/0.022 (no ring); total A 58042/57548 vs 59334/59354; cells 80/72 vs 71/68; A per cell 729/807 vs 847/884; food in cells 1.17-1.18 vs 1.15

limits: Two seeds, one parameter point; the ring here is energetic (no explicit permeability rule), so a world in which M raises the hop barrier for A (Ono-Ikegami's anisotropic repulsion) might give a working wall; 'leak' is the mean A at least 3 px from any cell.
